correctness.rationale: For n>=6 and 3<=k<=n-3, the one-deleted-basis polytope is exactly the hypersimplex clipped by x(H)<=k-1, where the cut passes through all k(n-k) adjacent vertices and creates no fractional vertices. At each surviving vertex B the normal cone has n primitive signed-coordinate rays, plus h=sum_{i in H}e_i only at |B∩H|=k-1. In N=Z^n/Z(1,...,1), M={m:sum m=0}, the signed-coordinate divisor map has saturated image; the extra-ray coordinate is an integral linear combination of coordinates, giving Cl=Z or Z² without torsion. Its unique Q-Cartier canonical character has m_i=+1 for i∈B, -1 otherwise, whence n=2k and, at new-facet vertices, k-2=1. This proves local criterion, all singular fixed points, and global iff (n,k)=(6,3). The exact-rational CHECKER.py inspected tests only n=6..9 and cannot replace the lattice proof.
